## Reader Contract

This chapter teaches the calculation pathway by which image points can constrain camera geometry.
It is not a calibration service, a qualified lab procedure, or evidence that a physical camera rig
is accurate. In this chapter, **self-calibration** means that a lab can learn or refine camera poses
from governed calibration observations instead of measuring every camera location by hand. It does
not mean that arbitrary video makes every intrinsic and extrinsic parameter observable.

The implementation boundary is intentionally strict:

| Component | Owning Authority | State on 2026-08-26 | What This Chapter May Do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intrinsic calibration contract | [Tools #4714](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/issues/4714) | `unavailable` | Explain equations and verify a synthetic model scenario |
| Extrinsic and flexible-layout calibration contract | [Tools #4721](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/issues/4721) | `unavailable` | Explain equations and rejection states |
| Calibration execution and lab workflow | UpstreamDrift | Not supplied by this slice | Describe required evidence only |
| Public pedagogy and sanitized fixture | AffineDrift | Available | Publish calculations without runtime authority |

Both Tools dependencies have status: `unavailable`, with null protected revision, schema identifier,
and fixture digest. The adapter fails closed if a future `available` state lacks all three immutable
pins. Consequently, this chapter does **not** claim parity with Tools fixtures, calibration approval,
or completion of AffineDrift issue #3962.

::: {.callout-warning title="No Calibration Approval"}
The executable fixture is classified `model_scenario`. Its exact arithmetic proves that the written
equations and coordinate conventions agree with a small synthetic example. It cannot qualify a
lens, camera, target, room, solver, synchronization system, or reconstructed motion.
:::

## In Layman's Terms

A camera flattens a three-dimensional scene onto a two-dimensional sensor. Calibration learns the
rules of that flattening: how the lens bends rays, where the image centre lies, and where the camera
was pointing. Multiple cameras can locate a point in space only when they see the *same point at the
same time* and their geometry is known well enough.

The difficult part is not asking an optimizer for numbers. The difficult part is knowing whether the
images contain enough independent information to determine those numbers. A solver can return a
small residual even when scale is free, a target was seen only head-on, two cameras moved together,
or timestamps refer to different instants. This manual treats an unobservable answer as unavailable,
not as a weakly supported number.

## Coordinate, Frame, and Unit Contract

The synthetic fixture freezes one convention so that every sign is testable:

- world and camera frames are right-handed, with (x) right, (y) down, and (z) forward;
- world points are expressed in metres and transformed *from world to camera* by
  (mathbf X_c = Rmathbf X_w + mathbf t);
- image coordinates are pixel-centre coordinates, (u) right and (v) down;
- angles are radians unless a field explicitly says degrees; and
- intrinsic focal lengths and principal points are in pixels.

For a rigid rotation, (R^mathsf{T}R=I) and (det R=+1). The camera centre in world coordinates is

$$
\mathbf C_w = -R^\mathsf{T}\mathbf t.
$$ {#eq-camera-centre}

Confusing (mathbf t) with (mathbf C_w) is a common extrinsic-sign error. A system that stores a
camera-to-world transform must invert it at the adapter boundary rather than quietly relabel it.

## Intrinsics and Distortion

### Pinhole Intrinsic Matrix

For a camera-frame point (mathbf X_c=(X_c,Y_c,Z_c)^mathsf{T}) with (Z_c>0), normalized image
coordinates are

$$
x = \frac{X_c}{Z_c}, \qquad y = \frac{Y_c}{Z_c}.
$$ {#eq-normalized-image}

The upper-triangular intrinsic matrix is

$$
K =
\begin{bmatrix}
f_x & s & c_x \\
0 & f_y & c_y \\
0 & 0 & 1
\end{bmatrix},
$$ {#eq-intrinsic-matrix}

where (f_x,f_y) are focal lengths in pixels, (c_x,c_y) are the principal point, and (s) is
skew. Most modern sensors constrain (s=0), but that is a declared model choice rather than a fact
inferred from the symbol (K). The complete distortion-free projection is

$$
\lambda\widetilde{\mathbf x}=K[R\mid\mathbf t]\widetilde{\mathbf X}_w,
\qquad \lambda=Z_c.
$$ {#eq-camera-projection}

The current [OpenCV calibration reference](https://docs.opencv.org/4.13.0/d9/d0c/group__calib3d.html)
uses this world-to-camera convention and also warns that a non-monotonic radial mapping should be
treated as calibration failure. AffineDrift cites that interface for comparison; it does not make
OpenCV the missing Tools authority.

### Brown-Conrady Distortion

The teaching fixture uses five coefficients ordered
((k_1,k_2,p_1,p_2,k_3)). With (r^2=x^2+y^2),

$$
L(r)=1+k_1r^2+k_2r^4+k_3r^6,
$$ {#eq-radial-factor}

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_d &= xL(r)+2p_1xy+p_2(r^2+2x^2),\\
y_d &= yL(r)+p_1(r^2+2y^2)+2p_2xy.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-brown-conrady}

Pixels then follow from

$$
u=f_xx_d+sy_d+c_x, \qquad v=f_yy_d+c_y.
$$ {#eq-distorted-pixel}

The fixture probe uses ((x,y)=(0.4,-0.3)),
((k_1,k_2,p_1,p_2,k_3)=(-0.1,0.01,0.001,-0.002,0)), and
(f_x=f_y=800), ((c_x,c_y)=(640,360)). It deterministically obtains
((u,v)=(951.096,126.578)) pixels.

### Intrinsic Calibration Is a Model Fit

Known target points (mathbf X_j), observed pixels (mathbf z_{ij}), camera parameters
(oldsymbol\theta), and target pose (oldsymbol\xi_i) define residuals

$$
\mathbf r_{ij}=\mathbf z_{ij}-
\pi(\mathbf X_j;\boldsymbol\theta,\boldsymbol\xi_i).
$$ {#eq-intrinsic-residual}

A common estimate minimizes a weighted robust objective,

$$
\min_{\boldsymbol\theta,\{\boldsymbol\xi_i\}}
\sum_{i,j}\rho\!\left(\mathbf r_{ij}^\mathsf{T}
W_{ij}\mathbf r_{ij}\right).
$$ {#eq-intrinsic-objective}

[Zhang's planar-target method](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/a-flexible-new-technique-for-camera-calibration/)
uses multiple views of a plane at different orientations, a closed-form initialization, and nonlinear
refinement. A planar target is not automatically degenerate: varied orientations supply constraints
through multiple homographies. Repeated nearly fronto-parallel views, small image coverage, weak
corner localization, and an over-parameterized distortion model can still make parameters highly
correlated or practically unobservable.

Record every accepted and rejected image, target identity and dimensions, image mode, focus,
aperture, temperature where relevant, corner covariance, solver and version, initial state, robust
loss, parameter constraints, residual distribution, covariance method, and validity interval.

## Extrinsics

Extrinsics describe one camera's pose relative to the declared world frame. They are not properties
of the camera body alone: remounting the same camera changes (R,mathbf t), while changing focus can
change intrinsics without moving the housing.

The projection matrix

$$
P=K[R\mid\mathbf t]
$$ {#eq-projection-matrix}

has projective scale. If (K) is known and (R,mathbf t) are constrained to a rigid transform, the
pose has six local degrees of freedom. If (P) is estimated as an unconstrained (3\times4) matrix,
it has eleven degrees of freedom after removing scale. Those are different estimation problems and
must not share an unlabeled result field.

## Direct Linear Transform

<abbr title="Direct Linear Transform">DLT</abbr> begins with homogeneous image point
(widetilde{\mathbf x}), world point (widetilde{\mathbf X}), and
(widetilde{\mathbf x}\times(P\widetilde{\mathbf X})=0). Two independent rows per
correspondence yield

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathbf 0^\mathsf{T} & -w\widetilde{\mathbf X}^\mathsf{T} &
v\widetilde{\mathbf X}^\mathsf{T} \\
w\widetilde{\mathbf X}^\mathsf{T} & \mathbf 0^\mathsf{T} &
-u\widetilde{\mathbf X}^\mathsf{T}
\end{bmatrix}
\mathbf p=\mathbf 0,
$$ {#eq-dlt-rows}

where (mathbf p=\operatorname{vec}(P)). Stacking correspondences forms (A\mathbf p=0); the
right singular vector associated with the smallest singular value supplies a projective solution.

This is an initializer, not a complete calibration claim. Coordinates should be normalized before
forming (A); rank and singular-value separation must be reported; points behind the camera must be
rejected; and the result should be refined under a physically declared model. Unconstrained 3D DLT
is rank deficient when all control points are coplanar. A planar homography method is a different,
explicitly constrained problem and must not be described as if the rank deficiency disappeared.

## Perspective-n-Point

<abbr title="Perspective-n-Point">PnP</abbr> estimates a calibrated camera pose from known
three-dimensional points and their two-dimensional image correspondences:

$$
\min_{R\in SO(3),\mathbf t}
\sum_j \rho\!\left(
\left\|\mathbf z_j-\pi(K,R,\mathbf t,\mathbf X_j)\right\|^2_{W_j}
\right).
$$ {#eq-pnp-objective}

The [EPnP reference implementation and paper](https://github.com/cvlab-epfl/EPnP) describe an
(O(n)) initializer for (n\ge4), including planar and non-planar cases. That fact does not make all
four-point layouts equally conditioned. Nearly collinear points, small angular extent, planar mirror
hypotheses, mislabeled points, and points concentrated in one image region can produce ambiguity or
large uncertainty.

A robust operational pipeline therefore needs more than the word `solvePnP`: deterministic
hypothesis generation, a registered robust estimator, inlier provenance, cheirality checks, explicit
planarity classification, minimum spatial coverage, covariance or another uncertainty statement,
and a typed ambiguous/unavailable outcome. Tools M5 will own that runtime seam; this chapter does not.

## Bundle Adjustment

Bundle adjustment jointly refines cameras and three-dimensional structure. For camera parameters
(oldsymbol\theta_i), points (mathbf X_j), and observation set (mathcal O),

$$
\min_{\{\boldsymbol\theta_i\},\{\mathbf X_j\}}
\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal O}
\rho\!\left(
\mathbf r_{ij}^\mathsf{T}W_{ij}\mathbf r_{ij}
\right),
\quad
\mathbf r_{ij}=\mathbf z_{ij}-\pi(\boldsymbol\theta_i,\mathbf X_j).
$$ {#eq-bundle-adjustment}

[Triggs and colleagues' synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-44480-7_21) emphasizes cost
functions, sparse optimization, gauge invariance, and quality control. A modern implementation often
eliminates point increments through a Schur complement, but solver efficiency is secondary to a
correct state definition and observable gauge.

### Observability and Gauge Freedom

If every camera pose and every point is free, image reprojection is unchanged by a global similarity
transform: one global rotation, three-dimensional translation, and scale can move together. These
seven degrees of gauge freedom mean the normal matrix is singular unless the system fixes a datum.
Typical choices include fixing one camera pose and metric target scale, applying justified priors, or
holding a surveyed reference rigidly. A prior changes the problem; it must be reported as evidence,
not hidden as a numerical convenience.

For local parameter vector (oldsymbol\delta), linearized residuals satisfy

$$
\mathbf r(\boldsymbol\delta)\approx\mathbf r_0+J\boldsymbol\delta.
$$ {#eq-linearized-residual}

With observation weight (W), the information matrix is (H=J^\mathsf{T}WJ). Rank deficiency,
very small singular values, or a large condition number signal exact or practical unobservability.
The labels depend on declared scaling and thresholds, so a production implementation must preserve
the singular spectrum, parameter scaling, tolerance, and solver version.

### Arbitrary Camera Count Is a Graph Problem

A camera-agnostic rig is not merely an array of (N) camera records. Form a bipartite graph whose
vertices are cameras and calibration target poses; an edge means that a camera observed that target
pose. Disconnected components have independent gauges and cannot share one world frame. A weak bridge
through one poor view can make the graph connected while leaving relative pose poorly conditioned.

Qualification should therefore report:

- connected components and articulation points of the observation graph;
- target coverage across image radius, depth, and orientation;
- pairwise and multi-view ray-angle distributions in the intended volume;
- singular values or another registered observability metric;
- leave-one-camera and leave-one-target sensitivity; and
- whether every intended capture location is supported by at least two synchronized, qualified views.

Adding cameras can improve visibility and redundancy, but it can also add weakly synchronized data,
shared-host failures, reflections, and new unobservable parameter correlations. No algorithm should
infer qualification from camera count alone.

## Uncertainty Propagation

A residual is not an uncertainty bound. Under a local linear approximation and a correctly scaled
noise model, one covariance approximation is

$$
\Sigma_{\theta}\approx\widehat\sigma^2
(J^\mathsf{T}WJ)^{+},
$$ {#eq-parameter-covariance}

where (+) denotes an inverse only after gauge removal, or a Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse with its
null space explicitly retained. The approximation is model-conditioned: wrong correspondences,
target deformation, lens changes, rolling-shutter effects, synchronization error, and pose-model bias
are not repaired by multiplying a Jacobian.

For a derived quantity (mathbf y=g(\boldsymbol\theta)), first-order propagation is

$$
\Sigma_y\approx G\Sigma_{\theta}G^\mathsf{T},
\qquad G=\left.\frac{\partial g}{\partial\boldsymbol\theta}\right|_{\widehat\theta}.
$$ {#eq-uncertainty-propagation}

### Rectified Stereo Example

For rectified cameras with focal length (f), baseline (B), and disparity (d=u_L-u_R),

$$
z=\frac{fB}{d}.
$$ {#eq-stereo-depth}

If the two horizontal pixel observations have independent standard deviation (sigma_p), then
(sigma_d=\sqrt2\sigma_p) and

$$
\sigma_z\approx
\left|\frac{\partial z}{\partial d}\right|\sigma_d
=\frac{z^2}{fB}\sqrt2\sigma_p.
$$ {#eq-stereo-depth-uncertainty}

The fixture uses (f=800\) pixels, (B=1\) metre, (d=160\) pixels, and
(sigma_p=0.5\) pixel. It obtains (z=5\) metres and
(sigma_z\approx0.0220971\) metre. This is a first-order image-noise result, not total lab accuracy.
It excludes calibration covariance, timing, target error, pose inference, and model inadequacy.

## Unsynchronized Observations

Two rays triangulate one moving point only if they refer to the same physical time. For local speed
(v) and exposure-time offset (Delta t), the first spatial inconsistency screen is

$$
\Delta s\approx v\lvert\Delta t\rvert.
$$ {#eq-synchronization-spatial-error}

At (8\) metres per second and (3\) milliseconds, the offset is (0.024\) metre. The synthetic
probe has a (1\)-millisecond registered limit and therefore returns `reject`. Reprojection
optimization must not absorb timing error into camera pose or distortion. If clocks, exposure starts,
or frame identity are unavailable, a dynamic multi-view result is unavailable even when static
geometry is excellent.

The timing record needs clock domain, timestamp origin, exposure start or midpoint convention,
trigger topology, measured skew, drift, dropped and duplicate frames, and uncertainty. Software
arrival times are not interchangeable with exposure times.

## Movement Rejection and Recalibration

Calibration validity belongs to a specific immutable camera identity, lens, focus, image mode,
mounting state, and interval. A camera can move while still producing plausible images. The system
therefore needs independent sentinels: fixed control points, surveyed fiducials, mount sensors, or a
registered background geometry check.

For baseline and observed poses (T_0,T_1\in SE(3)), define

$$
\Delta T=T_1T_0^{-1},\qquad
\Delta r=\lVert\operatorname{Log}(\Delta R)\rVert,
$$ {#eq-pose-change}

with translation evaluated in a declared frame. Thresholds must come from qualification and include
sentinel uncertainty; they are not universal constants. The fixture illustrates a camera-centre
shift of (0.015\) metre against a (0.01\)-metre model-scenario limit. Its state becomes
`invalidated`, and its action is `reject_and_recalibrate`.

### Recalibration State Machine

1. `unavailable`: required identity, intrinsic, extrinsic, synchronization, or provenance is absent.
2. `candidate`: observations exist but have not passed degeneracy and residual gates.
3. `qualified`: exact input, solver, uncertainty, validity, and approval records pass.
4. `suspect`: a sentinel, clock, device, lens, focus, or mode change crosses a registered warning.
5. `invalidated`: movement, identity mismatch, expired validity, or failed sentinel crosses a rejection
   gate; reconstruction stops.
6. `recalibrating`: new observations are collected under a new attempt identifier. The previous
   calibration remains immutable.

Cancellation never promotes a candidate. Recovery resumes only from durable, checksummed
observations and records the solver attempt separately. A successful recalibration creates a new
calibration identifier and validity interval; it does not overwrite the old record.

## Executable Pinned Fixture

The canonical synthetic input is
[`camera_geometry_fixture_v1.json`](../data/markerless_mocap/camera_geometry_fixture_v1.json), with
its adjacent SHA-256 lock. The versioned schema is
[`mocap_camera_geometry_fixture_v1.schema.json`](../schemas/mocap_camera_geometry_fixture_v1.schema.json).
The verifier is deliberately split into a strict contract adapter and small dependency-free equation
functions:

```text
python3 scripts/verify_mocap_camera_geometry_fixture.py \
  data/markerless_mocap/camera_geometry_fixture_v1.json
```

Its accepted result reports two cameras, six observations, and zero of two runtime dependencies
available. It independently recomputes all projected pixels, the Brown-Conrady probe, rectified
stereo depth and first-order uncertainty, synchronization rejection, and movement invalidation.

The fixture contains three world points and two idealized cameras with (f_x=f_y=800\) pixels.
Camera 0 is at the world origin; camera 1 has centre ((1,0,0)\) metres and therefore
(mathbf t=(-1,0,0)) under the declared world-to-camera convention. Point
((-0.5,0,5)) projects to (u=560) pixels in camera 0 and (u=400) pixels in camera 1, giving the
160-pixel disparity used above.

## Failure and Availability Matrix

| Condition | Required State | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tools M4 or M5 has no protected schema, revision, and fixture digest | `unavailable` | A moving issue or branch is not runtime authority |
| Point has (Z_c\le0) | `rejected` | The declared pinhole projection is invalid behind the camera |
| Unconstrained DLT control points are coplanar | `unavailable` | The design matrix lacks required rank |
| PnP yields unresolved physical hypotheses | `ambiguous` | A low residual does not choose a unique pose |
| Bundle adjustment gauge is not fixed | `unavailable` | Covariance and absolute pose are undefined |
| Observation graph is disconnected | `unavailable` per component | Components do not share one determined world frame |
| Exposure skew exceeds the registered dynamic limit | `rejected` | Rays describe different physical states |
| Camera movement exceeds a qualified sentinel limit | `invalidated` | Stored extrinsics no longer describe the camera |
| Required provenance, identity, units, or frame is absent | `unavailable` | Silent defaults would create an untraceable result |

## Commissioning Evidence Required Later

When Tools M4 and M5 are protected and versioned, AffineDrift can replace null dependency pins only
after a consumer contract test verifies the exact public schema and sanitized fixture digest. That
future gate must compare, at minimum:

- intrinsic and distortion parameter ordering, image-size scaling, camera identity, covariance, and
  validity semantics;
- world/camera transform direction, handedness, image axes, units, timestamp meaning, and camera
  centre derivation;
- DLT/PnP initialization, robust-estimator identity, degeneracy labels, cheirality, and inlier
  provenance;
- bundle-adjustment gauge, loss, constraints, convergence, singular spectrum, covariance method,
  and deterministic solver version;
- arbitrary-(N) observation-graph connectivity and partial-camera availability;
- movement sentinel thresholds, invalidation, cancellation, recovery, and immutable recalibration;
  and
- a public, sanitized example proving that unavailable and unsynchronized paths fail closed.

Physical commissioning additionally needs target metrology, repeated calibration across the full
volume, holdout reprojection tests, independent length and trajectory references, thermal and focus
sensitivity, deliberate mount-movement challenges, clock-skew injection, and comparison to the
actual downstream pose and C3D pathway. Training residuals alone are not validation.

## Current Limitations

- Tools #4714 and Tools #4721 remain unavailable dependencies; no runtime schema or fixture is pinned.
- The fixture uses ideal rigid cameras, a five-coefficient distortion model, and three synthetic
  points. It is not a general DLT, PnP, bundle-adjustment, or autocalibration solver.
- The uncertainty probe includes only independent horizontal pixel noise in rectified stereo.
- Movement and synchronization thresholds are model-scenario values, not shop qualification limits.
- No physical camera, target, timestamp, image, pose estimate, C3D file, or human-subject data is
  consumed or approved by this chapter.
- PDF, DOCX, LaTeX, and rendered-page parity remain pending while the workstation capacity drain
  prohibits rendering.

The source slice is complete only as bounded pedagogy. AFF-M2 remains open until the missing Tools
dependencies are protected, consumer parity is demonstrated, all required renders are produced and
inspected, protected checks pass, and a reviewed implementation is merged.
